description: A deciduous oak 10-25 m tall with dark, almost black, deeply cracked bark and big leaves, 10-20 cm long, cut into deep lobes that end in sharp bristles. It grows in the upper foothills from about 500 m up, among ponderosa pines and incense cedars; its new leaves come out pink in spring, it turns yellow and orange in fall, and its acorns were the favourite food of the Miwok, Maidu and Washoe people.

season_notes.winter: Bare: dark trunks and crooked grey limbs among the evergreen pines and cedars.
season_notes.spring: The new leaves unfold soft, velvety and pink to red (April-May), with hanging yellow catkins, then turn bright green.
season_notes.summer: Glossy yellow-green leaves; acorns from last year's flowers swell in their deep scaly cups.
season_notes.fall: Acorns drop (September-November) and the leaves turn yellow, gold and orange-brown before falling.

notes: California black oak is the oak of the lower conifer forest: 9-25 m (FEIS; to 36 m), here 10-22 m in the file with a veteran class to 26 m, dbh 0.3-1.4 m (radius_ratio 0.042). Around Placerville it comes in from about 500 m and is common from 600-900 m up with ponderosa pine and incense cedar, often on the deeper soils of slopes and benches. Decurrent Rauh's model, but more upright than the valley oaks: in the open a clean bole and a broad, rounded crown (photo W/H 0.9-1.2), in stands a narrow crown on a bole clear for 6-12 m (young class: W/H about 0.6); old trees often fork and go hollow (split_prob 0.45, veterans 0.8). Fire kills the top and the root crown sprouts a clump of stems (sprout clump class, 12%). Bark smooth grey on young stems; dark grey to nearly black on old trunks, deeply fissured into small irregular plates ('platy', bark_rgb about (78, 74, 70)). Leaves 10-20 cm, deeply cut into 7 lobes (three a side and the tip), each lobe ending in one to four bristle tips, glossy yellow-green above: leaf_shape lobed_large with lobes 7 at leaf_size_m 0.15, so cards are larger (cluster_m 1.5) and fewer. Deciduous and late to leaf: the new leaves come out velvety pink to red in April-May (spring colour a pink-green mix, leaf_on.spring 0.85), turn yellow-green by June, and turn yellow to orange-brown in October-November (fall colour from the photographs, leaf_on.fall 0.75, leaf_on_var 0.6: trees turn at different times). Oak mistletoe is fairly common. Acorns: yes, for the acorn game. 2.5-3 cm, deep scaly cup covering about half the nut, two seasons to ripen, drop September-November; Steller's jays, acorn woodpeckers, gray squirrels, deer and bears all eat them.
